WAIC from running sums

Source: R/mcmc_diag.R
compute_waic.Rd

The widely applicable information criterion (Watanabe 2010) of the Gaussian likelihood, computed from per-observation running sums kept during sampling, so it needs no saved draws. Fit with waic = TRUE and data_list.

Usage

compute_waic(fit, chain = NULL)

Arguments

fit

A multiggm_fit or multiggm_fit_list fitted with waic = TRUE.

chain

NULL (default) pools all chains.

Value

An object of class "multiggm_waic": a list with estimates (data frame with rows elpd_waic, p_waic, waic and columns estimate, se), by_group (the same per group) and pointwise (data frame with group, obs, elpd_waic, p_waic).

Details

For observation \(i\) with log-likelihood \(\ell_{is}\) at iteration \(s = 1, \dots, S\): \(\textrm{lppd}_i = \log(S^{-1} \sum_s e^{\ell_{is}})\), \(p_i = \textrm{var}_s(\ell_{is})\) and \(\textrm{elpd}_i = \textrm{lppd}_i - p_i\). WAIC is \(-2 \sum_i \textrm{elpd}_i\), lower is better. Use it to compare fits to the same data_list, for example different hyper settings, samplers, or a joint fit against separate fits per group (compare the per-group rows). The data are column-centered as for fitting. Observations with \(p_i > 0.4\) make WAIC unreliable (a warning is given); PSIS-LOO from the loo package is then preferable and needs saved draws.

References

Watanabe, S. (2010). Asymptotic equivalence of Bayes cross validation and widely applicable information criterion in singular learning theory. Journal of Machine Learning Research, 11, 3571-3594.

Vehtari, A., Gelman, A. & Gabry, J. (2017). Practical Bayesian model evaluation using leave-one-out cross-validation and WAIC. Statistics and Computing, 27, 1413-1432.

Examples

sim <- simulate_multiggm(K = 2, p = 6, n = 60, seed = 1)
fit <- multiggm_mcmc(data_list = sim$data_list, method = "ssvs",
                     burnin = 100, nsave = 100, save_draws = FALSE, waic = TRUE)
compute_waic(fit)
#> Warning: 21 of 120 observations have p_waic > 0.4; WAIC may be unreliable.
#> <multiggm_waic> computed from 120 observations
#>           estimate   se
#> elpd_waic  -1054.5 18.5
#> p_waic        28.3  2.6
#> waic        2109.0 37.0
